PostgreSQL menyimpan perubahan tabel dan: PostgreSQL stores table and index changes in data pages, but durability does not require every heap page to be written immediately at every commit. The write-ahead logging principle is that the change record must be written and flushed to durable storage before the data page containing the change may safely be written. If the server stops after the WAL flush but before the heap flush, recovery can read the WAL and perform REDO. A useful mental sequence is therefore: the change makes a buffer dirty, the WAL record receives an LSN position, the required WAL is flushed, and the data page may follow.
Commit acknowledgement bukan heap flush: Commit acknowledgement is not a heap flush
Pada mode synchronous commit lokal yang: In the usual local synchronous-commit mode, the server waits for the WAL commit record to be flushed to local storage according to configuration before reporting a successful COMMIT. It does not need to wait for every related heap and index page to be written at that moment. This is why a commit can be durable while buffers are still dirty: recovery will repeat the changes from WAL. Commit durability still depends on fsync, the WAL synchronization method, hardware, and correct configuration; one trace exercise does not prove anything about a storage device.
synchronous_commit = off mengurangi kepa: synchronous_commit = off reduces local certainty: the server can notify the client before the transaction WAL is flushed. A local crash can lose some transactions that were just reported successful, while the database is recovered to a consistent state rather than automatically becoming corrupt. This differs from asynchronous replication: replication describes when WAL is sent or applied on a standby, while synchronous_commit controls when the primary acknowledges a commit. Do not equate local commit, remote write, and remote apply without naming the chosen contract.
Recovery PostgreSQL menggunakan WAL untu: PostgreSQL recovery uses WAL to repeat the changes needed since the redo point. REDO is not a generic undo log that must reverse every unfinished statement. Data records can be replayed to make a page consistent, and then transaction status and MVCC rules determine whether a tuple is visible to a snapshot. If WAL contains a transaction change but no durable commit record, that change must not be read as a committed row after recovery. If a commit record exists, the change can become visible according to the snapshot and visibility rules.
Redo harus aman ketika recovery memprose: REDO must be safe while recovery processes records in LSN order and checks the relevant page state; the authored trace uses the phrase redo once only to teach ordering, not to implement a simulator. WAL also does not cancel a webhook, provider transfer, or side effect outside the database. After a crash, an external effect with an unknown outcome requires a business key, idempotency, and reconciliation. TEMP and unlogged relations are important exceptions: they are not places to store facts that require crash durability or replication.

Checkpoint adalah redo anchor: A checkpoint is a redo anchor
Checkpoint menandai titik dalam urutan W: A checkpoint marks a point in WAL order at which heap and index data files have been updated with information from before that point, and then a checkpoint record is written to WAL. Recovery can start REDO from the redo record associated with the latest checkpoint because changes before that point are guaranteed to be reflected in the data files. This does not mean every transaction must wait for the checkpoint. A normal commit can receive acknowledgement after its WAL commit is durable while dirty data pages continue waiting for the checkpointer or background writer.
Checkpoint juga bukan sinonim backup dan: A checkpoint is also not a synonym for a backup and is not proof that all old WAL is safe to delete without considering archiving or replicas. More frequent checkpoints reduce the amount of WAL that must be scanned after a crash, but force dirty pages to be written more often and can add I/O. The lesson trace names events and flush status explicitly so the learner reasons about the checkpoint's role rather than memorizing an interval number.
fsync mengatur apakah PostgreSQL berusah: fsync controls whether PostgreSQL tries to ensure updates are actually written to storage through fsync or an equivalent method. With fsync enabled, the cluster can recover consistently after an OS or hardware crash according to the storage contract. Turning fsync off is not a safe experiment for a database containing important data: failure can cause corruption that WAL cannot repair. This lesson provides no setting-change runbook and does not recommend a toggle without authorization and a disposable cluster.
full_page_writes melindungi kasus torn p: full_page_writes protects against a torn page. After a checkpoint, the first change to a page can write a full-page image to WAL. If power loss leaves only part of a disk page written, producing a mix of old and new bytes, row-level WAL alone may not be enough; the full image lets recovery restore a consistent page. The cost is more WAL and I/O, especially after a checkpoint. Do not treat full_page_writes as a hardware guarantee without data checksums, a storage contract, and operational evidence.
Membaca trade-off tanpa mengubah server: Reading trade-offs without changing the server
Trace authored memperlihatkan transactio: The authored trace shows transaction A committing before a checkpoint, then the checkpoint writing dirty pages and a redo anchor, followed by transaction B changing a page after the checkpoint. If a crash happens after A's commit but before the checkpoint, recovery can still start from the previous checkpoint and REDO A's WAL. If a crash happens after the checkpoint, recovery starts from the new anchor and must account for the full-page image on the first page change after the checkpoint. No trace number should be read as device latency, flush count, or a universal default.
Checkpoint timeout dan max_wal_size adal: checkpoint_timeout and max_wal_size are operational policies that must be weighed with recovery time, I/O load, WAL volume, and storage capacity. Reducing the interval can shorten REDO but adds flush work and full-page images. Synchronous commit off remains different: it makes a commit acknowledgement vulnerable to loss before the WAL flush, while a checkpoint governs data-page progress and the redo anchor. Production choices need review, observability, and change control; this lesson only trains a causal model.

A checkpoint is not a snapshot containing every business decision; it supplies a redo record so recovery does not need to scan the entire history. WAL records can contain heap or index page changes, and recovery repeats the needed changes according to LSN order and page metadata. Replaying the same record must not duplicate a row or payment; REDO uses record/page identity and must be idempotent on already-processed state. Idempotent here refers to recovery of a physical record, not permission for an application to repeat a provider charge. Retrying an external effect needs its own key and reconciliation.
PostgreSQL bukan mengandalkan generic UN: PostgreSQL does not rely on a generic UNDO log that reverses every change from an uncommitted transaction. Recovery can REDO recorded data-page changes while commit status and MVCC determine what a snapshot sees. Transaction A with a heap change and commit record can be visible after recovery. Transaction B with only a heap change can leave physical artifacts that are not visible as a committed row until cleanup follows PostgreSQL's lifecycle. What matters to a query is commit visibility, not an assumption that every uncommitted byte is immediately removed.
Synchronous replication memberi dimensi: Synchronous replication adds another dimension: a standby can receive and replay a record before the commit record makes the effect visible to a snapshot, because MVCC holds visibility until the commit is applied. This does not prove that the primary and standby have the same latency, and does not prove that an external provider received the effect. The recovery mental model must separate durable WAL, physical REDO, transaction visibility, and external acknowledgement.

Use payment identity, an idempotency key, an outbox/inbox protocol, and status reconciliation before retrying. Even if the local transaction appears rolled back, the external effect can remain and must be handled as a cross-system state.

Jelaskan urutan checkpoint–REDO–commit v: Explain the checkpoint–REDO–commit-visibility sequence in PostgreSQL recovery. Distinguish idempotent physical replay from a payment retry, then state why unlogged/TEMP and external effects limit the lesson's conclusions.
Trace memperlihatkan WAL change dan comm: The trace places durable WAL change and commit records before the heap-page flush. At step 3 the commit record is durable, allowing recovery to preserve transaction visibility; step 4 shows the heap page catching up. authored_position is an illustrative ordering label: a heap flush is not a WAL record and its label is not a separate record LSN. This is not pg_current_wal_lsn output or a disk measurement.
Event 2 menunjukkan commit A authored du: Event 2 shows authored commit A durable before the checkpoint. Event 3 marks checkpoint completion and progress of the redo point. The checkpoint record stores a pointer to a redo point that may precede the record itself; label 0/300 does not require REDO to start there. authored_position is only a practice ordering label. Event 4 shows a full-page image on the first change after the checkpoint; event 5 does not wait for the next checkpoint. No I/O or server behavior was observed.
TEMP bersifat session-local dan perubaha: TEMP is session-local and its data changes do not use normal WAL. UNLOGGED is a distinct persistent-relation mode with crash-recovery and replication limits. Neither proves logged-data durability in this exercise.
Trace dibaca berurutan: heap change 900: Read the trace in order: heap changes for 900 and 902 have not yet seen a commit and are not visible; their subsequent commit records change that state. The final report uses BOOL_OR(commit_record_seen) over all transaction records: 900 and 902 are visible, while 901 remains invisible. This is a simplified model of inserted transactions that commit or abort, with no later delete or update. The external effect for 902 remains unknown-reconcile. All results are authored rather than crash-recovery output.
Kolom authored_position memakai label be: The authored_position column uses LSN-like labels such as 0/100 and 0/150 to order the exercise. These are not WAL positions read from a server; in particular, the heap-flush event does not claim a separate WAL record. The learner separates three questions: whether WAL is durable, whether the heap page has caught up, and whether the transaction has a durable commit record. Change WAL without a commit record does not make the row committed. Conversely, an unflushed heap page does not mean a commit is lost if its commit WAL is durable.
